To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FAAH-2 is a novel enzyme that mediates NAE inactivation at lipid droplets in higher mammals.

1) FAAH-2, a newly identified NAE-catabolic enzyme, is localized to lipid droplets and is active at these sites; 2) NAEs, including AEA and PDE, are trafficked to lipid-droplets; and 3) FAAH-1, which is localized to the ER, is also active on lipid droplets.
FAAH-2 is a bona fide NAE hydrolyzing enzyme and that lipid droplets are novel sites of N-Acyl Ethanolamine (NAE) inactivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of FAAH-1 and FAAH-2.
the identification and characterization of the enzyme that mediates the inactivation of the bioactive lipid anandamide (AEA).
the biochemistry, cellular distribution, and physiological roles of N-acyletholandamides (NAEs).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the FAAH-2 is a bona fide NAE hydrolyzing enzyme, which is localized on lipid droplet organelles and can mediate N-acyl ethanolamide inactivation.
FAAH-2 is a bona fide NAE-hydrolyzing enzyme and that NAE inactiva-tion is spatially segregated to distinct cellular organelles.
FAAH-2 is an enzyme that is capable of hydrolyzing NAEs in the presence of lipid droplets, and the activity is dependent on lipid droplet localization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipid droplets represent novel, functional sites of N-acyletholandmine inactivation by fatty acid amide-hydrolase-2.
we have characterized a second enzyme capable of inactivating NAEs in humans and demonstrated that this enzyme localizes to lipid droplets.
FAAH-2 is a novel NAE-catabolic enzyme that is localized to lipid droplets in cells and that FAAH-1 and FAAH-2 may have distinct roles in NAE catabolic regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FAAH-2 is not a minor player in NAE inactivation, but rather an enzyme that may contribute to the catabolism of NAEs in vivo.
FAAH-2 is a bona fide NAE hydrolyzing enzyme that is localized on lipid droplet organelles in cells.
FAAH-2 is an enzyme that can hydrolyze N-acylethanoamines, such as anandamide and palmitoilethanolamide, in cells and that it is localized in lipid droplets.
